# Diagnostics

Error and lint codes reported by `kinemo check`, the preview and the build.

Every problem kinemo reports has a stable code: `K` codes are errors, `W` codes are lints (warnings; `kinemo check --strict` treats them as errors). Codes never change meaning and are never reused. `kinemo explain <code>` prints the same explanation in the terminal and `kinemo check --fix` applies the safe fixes. A lint can be allowed on one line with `# kinemo: allow W1002` or for the whole project in `kinemo.toml` ([`[lints] allow`](configuration.md#keys)).

| Code | Severity | Title |

*Error.* The scene code raised an ordinary Python exception.

<a id="range-01"></a>
## K01xx: Object lifecycle

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K0101`](#k0101) | error | object not in the scene |
| [`K0102`](#k0102) | error | object already removed |
| [`K0103`](#k0103) | error | object with two parents |
| [`K0104`](#k0104) | error | outside scene construction |
| [`K0105`](#k0105) | error | invalid argument |
| [`K0106`](#k0106) | error | unknown prop |
| [`W0110`](#w0110) | warning (lint) | play with at= |

<a id="k0101"></a>
### K0101: object not in the scene

*Error.* Creating an object does not put it in the scene. `.to()` only animates objects that have entered, via `s.add(obj)` or an entrance verb (`k.draw`, `k.write`, `k.fade_in`, `k.grow`).

Example that triggers it:

```python
c = k.Circle()
s.play(c.to(x=2))
```

Fix:

```python
s.play(k.draw(c))
s.play(c.to(x=2))
```

<a id="k0102"></a>
### K0102: object already removed

*Error.* The object left the scene (`s.remove`, `k.fade_out`, `k.shrink`) before the animation's time. Bring it back with an entrance verb or animate it before it exits.

<a id="k0103"></a>
### K0103: object with two parents

*Error.* An object belongs to exactly one group. To show the same visual in two places, copy it (`obj.copy()`); to change groups while keeping its position, use `k.reparent(obj, new_parent)`.

<a id="k0104"></a>
### K0104: outside scene construction

*Error.* Objects, signals and animations belong to a scene. Create them inside the function decorated with `@k.scene` (or inside a clip, a handler or a component's `build()`).

<a id="k0105"></a>
### K0105: invalid argument

*Error.* An argument has a type or value the API does not accept.

<a id="k0106"></a>
### K0106: unknown prop

*Error.* The object has no such prop. See `kinemo docs <Type>`.

<a id="w0110"></a>
### W0110: play with at=

*Warning (lint).* `play(..., at=)` does not move the cursor; use `s.start(..., at=)` to make that explicit.

<a id="range-02"></a>
## K02xx / W02xx: Animations, conflicts, interpolation

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K0201`](#k0201) | error | two animations on the same prop |
| [`K0202`](#k0202) | error | invalid duration |
| [`K0203`](#k0203) | error | not an animation |
| [`K0204`](#k0204) | error | non-reversible animation in during |
| [`K0205`](#k0205) | error | type without interpolation |

<a id="k0201"></a>
### K0201: two animations on the same prop

*Error.* Two animations write the same prop of the same object over overlapping intervals. Chain them (`k.seq`) or, if summing them is intended, use `blend="add"` on the second one.

<a id="k0202"></a>
### K0202: invalid duration

*Error.* Durations and waits must be finite, non-negative numbers.

<a id="k0203"></a>
### K0203: not an animation

*Error.* `s.play`/`s.start` take `k.Animation` values (verbs, `.to()`, clips).

<a id="k0204"></a>
### K0204: non-reversible animation in during

*Error.* `s.during` reverts what it applied when the block ends; it only accepts state changes (`.to`) and `k.indicate`. Entrance/exit verbs have no reverse.

<a id="k0205"></a>
### K0205: type without interpolation

*Error.* Lists and custom types must declare how to interpolate: `k.signal([...], lerp=k.lerp.pointwise)` or `lerp=None` to switch in a single step.

<a id="range-03"></a>
## K03xx / W03xx: Reactive system

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K0301`](#k0301) | error | tracked read outside a reactive context |
| [`K0302`](#k0302) | error | x.now inside a lambda |
| [`K0303`](#k0303) | error | derived values are read-only |
| [`K0304`](#k0304) | error | signal used as a boolean |
| [`K0305`](#k0305) | error | signal converted to a number |
| [`K0306`](#k0306) | error | write inside a derived value |
| [`K0310`](#k0310) | error | untraceable function |
| [`W0310`](#w0310) | warning (lint) | lambda in a loop |
| [`W0311`](#w0311) | warning (lint) | captured Python list |
| [`W0312`](#w0312) | warning (lint) | eased clock |

<a id="k0301"></a>
### K0301: tracked read outside a reactive context

*Error.* `x()` only works inside prop lambdas, `k.computed` and `.map` functions. In the scene body, read the value at the cursor with `x.now`.

<a id="k0302"></a>
### K0302: x.now inside a lambda

*Error.* `x.now` inside a lambda would freeze the value at build time. Use `x()` so the lambda follows the signal.

<a id="k0303"></a>
### K0303: derived values are read-only

*Error.* Derived values are recomputed from their sources; animate the source.

<a id="k0304"></a>
### K0304: signal used as a boolean

*Error.* `if signal:` has no single value: the signal changes over time. Use `x.now > 2` to decide at the cursor, or `k.when(x > 2, ...)` to react during playback.

<a id="k0305"></a>
### K0305: signal converted to a number

*Error.* Functions like `math.sin` need a number; a signal is a value over time. Use `k.sin(x)` (native) or `x.map(k.python(math.sin))`.

<a id="k0306"></a>
### K0306: write inside a derived value

*Error.* Derived values are pure: they do not write to signals.

<a id="k0310"></a>
### K0310: untraceable function

*Error.* The function uses something that cannot be compiled to the IR (math.*, if on a symbolic value, external libraries). Replace it with the native `k` building blocks or accept the cost with `k.python(fn)`.

<a id="w0310"></a>
### W0310: lambda in a loop

*Warning (lint).* The lambda captures the loop variable by reference; use `lambda i=i:` or `.map`.

<a id="w0311"></a>
### W0311: captured Python list

*Warning (lint).* Plain lists are not tracked; use `k.list([...])`.

<a id="w0312"></a>
### W0312: eased clock

*Warning (lint).* A signal used as a clock must advance linearly; use `k.time.map(...)`.

<a id="range-04"></a>
## K04xx: Layout and constraints

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K0401`](#k0401) | error | axis held by a constraint |
| [`K0402`](#k0402) | error | constraint cycle |
| [`K0403`](#k0403) | error | conflicting constraints |
| [`K0404`](#k0404) | error | unknown anchor |

<a id="k0401"></a>
### K0401: axis held by a constraint

*Error.* The object's position comes from a constraint (`place`, a container or a binding). Change the constraint with an animation via `.to_place(...)`, release it with `.to(..., unpin=True)` (or `.unpin()` at the cursor), or drop a binding with `.unbind()`.

<a id="k0402"></a>
### K0402: constraint cycle

*Error.* The constraints depend on each other in a cycle; break one of them.

<a id="k0403"></a>
### K0403: conflicting constraints

*Error.* Two constraints compete for the same axis. Remove one or mark the weaker one with `weak=True`.

<a id="k0404"></a>
### K0404: unknown anchor

*Error.* Valid anchors: center, top, bottom, left, right and combinations such as top-left.

<a id="k0601"></a>
### K0601: signal in a static field

*Error.* Declare the field as `k.Prop[T]` to accept reactive values.

<a id="k0602"></a>
### K0602: unassigned out

*Error.* Every `k.Out` must be assigned in `build()`.

## K07xx / W07xx: Events

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |

<a id="w0701"></a>
### W0701: handler object never removed

*Warning (lint).* Objects created in handlers should leave the scene.

<a id="k0702"></a>
### K0702: event did not happen before the timeout

*Error.* No trigger before the timeout.

<a id="k0703"></a>
### K0703: event already happened

*Error.* The event happened before the cursor; use `s.start` instead of the earlier `play`.

<a id="k0801"></a>
### K0801: unsupported LaTeX command

*Error.* Use `engine="tex"` for packages the built-in engine does not cover.

<a id="w0801"></a>
### W0801: morph without matches

*Warning (lint).* The shapes have nothing in common; the morph does a warp + crossfade.

<a id="k0802"></a>
### K0802: unknown code language

*Error.* `k.Code` highlights the languages listed in the message; `lang="text"` shows any code without colors.

## W10xx: Visual legibility

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`W1001`](#w1001) | warning (lint) | outside the safe area |
| [`W1002`](#w1002) | warning (lint) | text over text |
| [`W1003`](#w1003) | warning (lint) | low contrast |
| [`W1004`](#w1004) | warning (lint) | small text |
| [`W1005`](#w1005) | warning (lint) | invisible object |
| [`W1006`](#w1006) | warning (lint) | visual noise |
| [`W1007`](#w1007) | warning (lint) | static scene |

<a id="w1001"></a>
### W1001: outside the safe area

*Warning (lint).* The object extends beyond the frame's safe area. Objects entirely offstage are not reported; for one cropped on purpose, `bleed=True`.

<a id="w1002"></a>
### W1002: text over text

*Warning (lint).* Two texts overlap by more than 10% of their area.

<a id="w1003"></a>
### W1003: low contrast

*Warning (lint).* Contrast between text and what is behind it (the background, or a filled shape under it such as a card or a speech bubble) is below 4.5:1.

<a id="w1004"></a>
### W1004: small text

*Warning (lint).* Text smaller than 18 px at the final resolution.

<a id="w1005"></a>
### W1005: invisible object

*Warning (lint).* Object invisible for more than 3 s, never removed and not seen again.

<a id="w1006"></a>
### W1006: visual noise

*Warning (lint).* More than 12 short simultaneous animations.

<a id="w1007"></a>
### W1007: static scene

*Warning (lint).* More than 8 s without visual change.

## K11xx: Names from other libraries (Manim)

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K1101`](#k1101) | error | Manim name |
| [`K1102`](#k1102) | error | Manim `.animate` |
| [`K1103`](#k1103) | error | Manim `self.play` |
| [`K1104`](#k1104) | error | Manim ValueTracker |
| [`K1105`](#k1105) | error | Manim updater |
| [`K1106`](#k1106) | error | Manim direction constant |

<a id="k1101"></a>
### K1101: Manim name

*Error.* Manim verbs have a direct equivalent in `k.` (see the Manim → kinemo table).

<a id="k1102"></a>
### K1102: Manim `.animate`

*Error.* In kinemo, an animated state change is `s.play(obj.to(...))`.

<a id="k1103"></a>
### K1103: Manim `self.play`

*Error.* The scene receives `s: k.Scene`; use `s.play(...)`.

<a id="k1104"></a>
### K1104: Manim ValueTracker

*Error.* Use `k.signal(value)`.

<a id="k1105"></a>
### K1105: Manim updater

*Error.* Pass a signal or a lambda to the prop: `obj.set(x=other.x)`.

<a id="k1106"></a>
### K1106: Manim direction constant

*Error.* Position comes from constraints (`place`) or from `x=`/`y=`.

## K12xx: Data and interoperability (Arrow, arrays)

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K1201`](#k1201) | error | data without Arrow |
| [`K1202`](#k1202) | error | missing column |
| [`K1203`](#k1203) | error | column with the wrong type |
| [`K1204`](#k1204) | error | duplicate key |

<a id="k1201"></a>
### K1201: data without Arrow

*Error.* The object does not implement the Arrow PyCapsule Interface.

<a id="k1202"></a>
### K1202: missing column

*Error.* The table has no column with that name; check `x=`, `y=` and `key=`.

<a id="k1203"></a>
### K1203: column with the wrong type

*Error.* Chart values need a numeric column (int, float or decimal).

<a id="k1204"></a>
### K1204: duplicate key

*Error.* Each row of a chart needs a unique key (`key=`); aggregate the data or pick another column.

<a id="w1302"></a>
### W1302: k.python depending on a parameter

<a id="range-14"></a>
## W14xx: Audio and voice

| Code | Severity | Title |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`K1401`](#k1401) | error | TTS command failed |
| [`W1401`](#w1401) | warning (lint) | voice without a TTS provider |
| [`W1402`](#w1402) | warning (lint) | unknown TTS provider |
| [`W1403`](#w1403) | warning (lint) | content runs past the narration |
| [`W1404`](#w1404) | warning (lint) | stale narration |
| [`W1405`](#w1405) | hint (does not fail `--strict`) | narration without audio yet |

<a id="k1401"></a>
### K1401: TTS command failed

*Error.* The command provider (`[tts] provider = "command"`) has no command, could not start, exited with an error or wrote no audio. The message quotes the end of its error output.

Fix:

```python
Run the command by hand with a short text; check `[tts] command` in kinemo.toml.
```

<a id="w1401"></a>
### W1401: voice without a TTS provider

*Warning (lint).* No provider configured: silence with an estimated duration.

<a id="w1402"></a>
### W1402: unknown TTS provider

*Warning (lint).* `[tts] provider` in kinemo.toml names a provider that is not installed (a typo, or its package is missing): the voice becomes silence with an estimated duration.

Fix:

```python
Install `kinemo-tts-<name>`, or use one of the installed providers the message lists.
```

<a id="w1403"></a>
### W1403: content runs past the narration

*Warning (lint).* The animations inside a `with s.voice(...)` block last more than 0.25 s longer than its narration, so the next line starts late and the silence shows.

Fix:

```python
Shorten or speed up the animations, sync them to the line with `v.at(...)`, or lengthen the narration.
```

<a id="w1404"></a>
### W1404: stale narration

*Warning (lint).* A beat of a `k.Script` has recorded audio made from a different text (per `audio/manifest.json`): the script changed after the audio was made.

Fix:

```python
Make the audio again: `kinemo voice <scene file>` (only missing and stale beats), or `--force <id>`.
```

<a id="w1405"></a>
### W1405: narration without audio yet

*Hint (does not fail `--strict`).* A line has no audio and this build does not make it (`kinemo check` never does; `[tts] on_build = "estimate"`, the default for the command provider): its length is estimated from `[tts] wpm`.

Fix:

```python
`kinemo voice <scene file>` makes every missing line in one run; `kinemo render` makes them before rendering.
```
